editorial.headline: Burial and Cremation Services: Nationally Open, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity embraces burial, cremation and funeral-home services at every business scale—but its 100% national PMA ceiling does not permit foreign registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. Nationally, it is open to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. Bali reaches a different result: the activity is blocked for PMA under the province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. The record identifies the relevant trigger clearly: at the Large scale, every scope is assessed by OSS as Low or Medium-Low risk, placing it within Bali’s restriction introduced in May 2026.

The activity itself concerns the practical, continuing work around human or animal burial and cremation. It includes preparing a body for burial or cremation, embalming, and funeral-home attendant services; providing burial or cremation services; and renting equipped rooms in a funeral home. Its scope also extends beyond the immediate ceremony to the rental or sale of grave sites and the maintenance of graves, mausoleums, and other matters connected with the burial process in service of the public.

The national registration position is broad in enterprise scale. The record opens the activity to Micro, Small, Medium, and Large businesses, rather than reserving it for a particular size of operator. For PMA, the national position is equally direct: foreign ownership may reach 100%, with Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021 cited as the source. That national openness describes the foreign-investment ceiling; it does not override a provincial restriction that applies to the relevant risk class.

A national 100% ceiling does not create a PMA registration route in Bali. For an investor considering this activity elsewhere in Indonesia, the record presents a nationally open PMA position across all listed scales. For Bali, the decisive fact is the provincial block: the activity’s Low or Medium-Low OSS risk classification at the Large scale brings it under the permanent moratorium. The distinction is not cosmetic. It means that, despite national openness, a foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today.
